candidates.target: attn_dense_hd128_large4k (0.923), _seq8k (0.941), _hd192_dv128 (0.937), minor _seq16k (0.953)
candidates.lever: Causal persist work-ordering: global LPT (heaviest m-block across ALL heads first) instead of per-head LPT, matching FA3's DynamicPersistentTileScheduler
candidates.mechanism: ncu MEASURED: large4k persist runs at only 58.1% SM/compute (vs seq16k 73.3% on the IDENTICAL mainloop) with DRAM 7.8% — pure makespan tail, not memory. Our pf_work (kernels/fa3_hopper.cu:925-929) maps work->tile per-(bi,hk): work=bi*hb+hk*tiles_m+local, m_block=(tiles_m-1)-local. Heavies are front-loaded WITHIN each head but the LAST head's heavy m-block sits at work index total-tiles_m, so the greedy atomic (work_ctr) hands it out near the global tail -> one CTA runs a ~tiles_m-nblock heavy tile while ~131 CTAs drain the light tail and idle (overhang ~= heavy tile time). FA3's causal scheduler (tile_scheduler.hpp:293-314, get_block_coord) orders GLOBALLY: head varies fastest within an L2 section, m_block next (with block=num_m_blocks-1-block LPT), so the last tiles handed out are m_block=0 (lightest) across the section -> tail overhang ~= 1 n-block. Because these configs are compute-bound with 2.6-7.8% DRAM, the L2-section width can be all heads (degenerate swizzle) without a DRAM penalty; FA3 restricts to non-causal via StaticPersistentTileScheduler (launch_template:66-70), so keep our current per-head order for non-causal.
candidates.concrete_change: In pf_work (kernels/fa3_hopper.cu:918) add an `int batch` param (pass `batch` at both persist call sites 1560 and 1749; and fp8 sites 2212,2279). Replace lines 925-929 with a causal branch: `int bi,m_block; if(causal){ const int nhb=hkv*batch; const int m_local=work/nhb; const int hbrem=work-m_local*nhb; bi=hbrem/hkv; t.hk=hbrem-bi*hkv; m_block=(tiles_m-1)-m_local; } else { const int hb=tiles_m*hkv; bi=work/hb; const int rem=work-bi*hb; t.hk=rem/tiles_m; m_block=rem-t.hk*tiles_m; }` then use bi/m_block below. Keeps the dynamic greedy atomic (only the work->tile mapping changes; producer+consumer stay lock-step since both call pf_work). Optional FA3-exact refinement: section heads by swizzle=clamp(L2_bytes/(2*seqlen_k*(hd+hdv)*2),1,hkv) if any regression appears on a memory-heavier config, but profiles show it is unnecessary here.
